page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and secure virtualization via SVM.

This server configuration does not include a GPU, limiting its utility for hardware-accelerated graphics or native GPU-based deep learning. Additionally, local storage is restricted to a nominal 1 GB network-attached volume, meaning any data-intensive workloads will require external network storage solutions. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the vx1-g-64c-256g demonstrates top-tier performance. Its single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores, along with PassMark CPU and database operations, rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth for large blocks (both read and write) also falls into the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang show exceptional throughput. For lightweight machine learning, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds on small 135M LLM models, and strong performance on medium 7B models.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation and high resource density, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound, multi-threaded workloads that do not require massive local storage. It is highly suited for software compilation, large-scale web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
